8	# Svetra
9	
10	This project's data layer is designed in `svetra.yaml`. Svetra checks it, compiles it into Postgres with row-level security on every table, TypeScript and Zod types, sign-in settings and access tests, and explains it in plain English. **You design with the person; Svetra makes it safe; you build the rest.**
11	
12	Use the `svetra` MCP tools (`validate`, `compile`, `explain`, `context`, `graph`). If they aren't available, run the same commands with `npx -y svetra <command>`; add `--json` to `validate`.
13	
14	## The loop
15	
16	1. **Design first.** Turn the request into a change to `svetra.yaml`: entities, fields, policies, roles, `auth`, and holes only for logic that a policy can't express. Ask at most three questions, each with a recommended default, and only when the answer changes the design.
17	2. **Validate after every edit.** Fix every error using its `remediation.hint` before doing anything else. Never move on with errors. Warnings and info are worth reading: they usually point at a real gap.
18	3. **Plan a change** to an app that already exists (`svetra.yaml` is committed in git): call `plan` before compiling.
19	   - Tell the person every **destructive** line (data that would be deleted) and every **wider** line (people who'd see or change more), in their words.
20	   - Get their explicit yes in this conversation, then run `npx -y svetra plan --accept <kinds>`. Never accept on their behalf.
21	   - A rename is `was: <old name>` on the renamed entity or field, never a removal and an addition: that deletes every value.
22	4. **Compile.** Never edit what Svetra generates:
23	   - `supabase/schemas/svetra.sql`
24	   - `src/svetra.gen.ts`
25	   - `supabase/tests/svetra.test.sql`
26	   - the sign-in keys Svetra sets in `supabase/config.toml`
27	
28	   Change `svetra.yaml` and compile again instead.
29	5. **Write only hole bodies,** in `supabase/holes/<name>.sql` (PL/pgSQL). Inputs are `p_<input>`, and `p_caller` is the signed-in person's id. A hole can touch only the entities in its `reads` and `writes`, and its `when` already decides who may call it, so don't repeat that check in the body. To let people join a team or start one, give the hole `grants: [<role>]` and insert into `"svetra"."role_grants"` in the body; never grant roles from app code.
30	6. **Explain.** Call `explain` and tell the person what changed in their words: who can see and change what, and "Before going live" when there is one. Never paste SQL at them.
31	7. **Prove it.** If a local Supabase is running, `supabase test db` runs the access tests as real users. Report failures exactly as they are.
32	
33	## Rules
34	
35	- **Never** use the service role key in app code, and never turn row-level security off.
36	- **Never** weaken a rule to make a test pass. A failing access test means the design and the database disagree; find out which is wrong.
37	- **Prefer a policy over a hole, and a hole over app code,** for anything about who can see or change data.
38	- **App code calls holes** through the typed functions in `src/svetra.gen.ts`, such as `transfer(supabase, input)`.
39	- **Read the design with `context`**, not by opening the generated files.
40	- **When asked "who can see X?",** call `explain` again and answer from its lines, even if you called it earlier. Never answer from memory: the file may have changed since.
41	
42	## The format, briefly
43	
44	```yaml
45	svetra: "0.1"
46	system: Bookings
47	auth:
48	  sign_in: [email, google]
49	roles:
50	  admin: { description: "Runs the business", mfa: true }
51	  staff: { description: "Works at one location", scope: Location }
52	entities:
53	  Location:
54	    fields:
55	      id:   { type: uuid, primary: true }
56	      name: { type: text, required: true }
57	  Booking:
58	    fields:
59	      id:       { type: uuid, primary: true }
60	      customer: { type: user, required: true }
61	      location: { type: ref, entity: Location, required: true }
62	policies:
63	  customers_see_own:  { on: Booking, allow: [select, insert], when: "customer == auth.user" }
64	  staff_manage_local: { on: Booking, allow: [select, update], when: "has_role('staff', location)" }
65	  admins_run_locations: { on: Location, allow: [select, insert, update], when: "has_role('admin')" }
66	  staff_see_location: { on: Location, allow: [select], when: "has_role('staff', id)" }
67	holes:
68	  cancel:
69	    kind: function
70	    input: { booking: Booking.id }
71	    writes: [Booking]
72	    when: "booking.customer == auth.user"
73	```
74	
75	The full specification is at https://github.com/555aaditya/Svetra/tree/main/docs.

---
name: svetra
description: Design and change a Supabase app through svetra.yaml, the one file that decides its data, who can see and change what, roles, sign-in, and where custom code goes. Use whenever the person wants to add or change tables, fields, access rules, roles or teams, sign-in or two-factor settings, or server-side logic in a project that has svetra.yaml, and to answer "who can see X?".
---

<!-- Written by `svetra init`, and replaced each time it runs. Edit svetra.yaml, not this file. -->

# Svetra

This project's data layer is designed in `svetra.yaml`. Svetra checks it, compiles it into Postgres with row-level security on every table, TypeScript and Zod types, sign-in settings and access tests, and explains it in plain English. **You design with the person; Svetra makes it safe; you build the rest.**

Use the `svetra` MCP tools (`validate`, `compile`, `explain`, `context`, `graph`). If they aren't available, run the same commands with `npx -y svetra <command>`; add `--json` to `validate`.

## The loop

1. **Design first.** Turn the request into a change to `svetra.yaml`: entities, fields, policies, roles, `auth`, and holes only for logic that a policy can't express. Ask at most three questions, each with a recommended default, and only when the answer changes the design.
2. **Validate after every edit.** Fix every error using its `remediation.hint` before doing anything else. Never move on with errors. Warnings and info are worth reading: they usually point at a real gap.
3. **Plan a change** to an app that already exists (`svetra.yaml` is committed in git): call `plan` before compiling.
   - Tell the person every **destructive** line (data that would be deleted) and every **wider** line (people who'd see or change more), in their words.
   - Get their explicit yes in this conversation, then run `npx -y svetra plan --accept <kinds>`. Never accept on their behalf.
   - A rename is `was: <old name>` on the renamed entity or field, never a removal and an addition: that deletes every value.
4. **Compile.** Never edit what Svetra generates:
   - `supabase/schemas/svetra.sql`
   - `src/svetra.gen.ts`
   - `supabase/tests/svetra.test.sql`
   - the sign-in keys Svetra sets in `supabase/config.toml`

   Change `svetra.yaml` and compile again instead.
5. **Write only hole bodies,** in `supabase/holes/<name>.sql` (PL/pgSQL). Inputs are `p_<input>`, and `p_caller` is the signed-in person's id. A hole can touch only the entities in its `reads` and `writes`, and its `when` already decides who may call it, so don't repeat that check in the body. To let people join a team or start one, give the hole `grants: [<role>]` and insert into `"svetra"."role_grants"` in the body; never grant roles from app code.
6. **Explain.** Call `explain` and tell the person what changed in their words: who can see and change what, and "Before going live" when there is one. Never paste SQL at them.
7. **Prove it.** If a local Supabase is running, `supabase test db` runs the access tests as real users. Report failures exactly as they are.

## Rules

- **Never** use the service role key in app code, and never turn row-level security off.
- **Never** weaken a rule to make a test pass. A failing access test means the design and the database disagree; find out which is wrong.
- **Prefer a policy over a hole, and a hole over app code,** for anything about who can see or change data.
- **App code calls holes** through the typed functions in `src/svetra.gen.ts`, such as `transfer(supabase, input)`.
- **Read the design with `context`**, not by opening the generated files.
- **When asked "who can see X?",** call `explain` again and answer from its lines, even if you called it earlier. Never answer from memory: the file may have changed since.

## The format, briefly

```yaml
svetra: "0.1"
system: Bookings
auth:
  sign_in: [email, google]
roles:
  admin: { description: "Runs the business", mfa: true }
  staff: { description: "Works at one location", scope: Location }
entities:
  Location:
    fields:
      id:   { type: uuid, primary: true }
      name: { type: text, required: true }
  Booking:
    fields:
      id:       { type: uuid, primary: true }
      customer: { type: user, required: true }
      location: { type: ref, entity: Location, required: true }
policies:
  customers_see_own:  { on: Booking, allow: [select, insert], when: "customer == auth.user" }
  staff_manage_local: { on: Booking, allow: [select, update], when: "has_role('staff', location)" }
  admins_run_locations: { on: Location, allow: [select, insert, update], when: "has_role('admin')" }
  staff_see_location: { on: Location, allow: [select], when: "has_role('staff', id)" }
holes:
  cancel:
    kind: function
    input: { booking: Booking.id }
    writes: [Booking]
    when: "booking.customer == auth.user"
```

The full specification is at https://github.com/555aaditya/Svetra/tree/main/docs.

content.text:
The notes backend is in `supabase/migrations/20261116000000_notes.sql`. I haven't run it or the generated access tests, because no local Supabase was running.

- **Table:** `note` has `id` (uuid primary key, generated), `owner` (uuid, required, references `auth.users`) and `body` (text, required). There is an index on `owner`.
- **Who sees and changes what:** row-level security is on. Signed-in people can read, create, edit and delete only rows where `owner` is their own id. Creating or editing a note can't set `owner` to someone else. Anonymous visitors get nothing.

I put the design in `svetra.yaml` (renaming the template's `author` field to `owner`), validated it with no errors, and compiled it. The migration is a copy of the generated `supabase/schemas/svetra.sql`, so recompile and recopy it if the design changes. The compile also wrote `src/svetra.gen.ts` and `supabase/tests/svetra.test.sql`.
